newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Labour Court in bid to avert nurses' strike.
newsitem.headline: Irish Labour Court in bid to avert nurses' strike.

text.p: Ireland's Labour Court has invited health service employers and nurses' union leaders to exploratory talks on Tuesday in a bid to avert a planned nationwide strike.
The strike will be the first ever by Irish nurses if it goes ahead as planned from next Monday and will cause massive disruption to the health service.
It is expected to lead to the cancellation of routine hospital admissions and out-patient appointments and a withdrawal from non-nursing support work and administrative duties.

There is also growing uncertainty about the extent of emergency cover that will be provided in Dublin hospitals as local strike committees are reported to be reluctant to provide the levels of cover agreed by unions at national level.

The nurses, whose demands include early retirement at 55, better terms for staff nurses and those entering the profession and bonuses for those with additional qualifications, have already rejected a 50 million punt ($79.66 million) government offer.

Irish health minister Michael Noonan says the government cannot afford any more than what is on offer and is also worried that he could trigger a further round of public sector pay if he meets the nurses' demands.
The Labour Court said the talks would be of an informal nature to ascertain if the court could be of assistance in resolving the differences between the two sides.
"It is exploratory; we just want to see if there is anything to be gained by an intervention," Labour Court chairwoman Evelyn Owens said.
